newsitem.title: USA: Kaiser says Q1 net down on prices, shipments.
newsitem.headline: Kaiser says Q1 net down on prices, shipments.

text.p: Kaiser Aluminum Corp on Wednesday attributed lower first-quarter net to lower realized prices for alumina and fabricated aluminum, lower alumina shipments and higher interest expenses.

Kaiser's first quarter net fell to $2.6 million, or $0.01 per common share, for the first quarter of 1997, from net income of $9.9 million, or $0.11 per common share, for the same period of 1996. Net sales rose to $547.4 million from $531.1.

"Relative to the year-ago quarter, net income for the first quarter of 1997 was down due largely to the unfavorable impact of lower realized prices for alumina and fabricated aluminum products, lower shipments of alumina, and higher interest expense, offset in part by increased shipments of fabricated aluminum products," said chairman and chief executive George Haymaker Jr.

But Haymaker said results rose from a $3.3 million net loss in the 1996 fourth quarter "due to an increase in realized prices in all three of Kaiser's key product areas -- alumina, primary aluminum, and fabricated aluminum products -- along with improved cost performance, especially in our alumina and flat-rolled products operations."
